chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Hadid, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked: A man buys goods from another man, then leaves them with him and says, 'I will bring you their price.' He (the Imam) said: 'If he comes within the time between them and three days, [the sale is valid]; otherwise, there is no sale for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a sale where the buyer takes the item but pays later?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a three-day grace period for payment in deferred transactions, a ruling derived from the practice of the Prophet and early Imams to prevent disputes over ownership transfer. In Shia jurisprudence, this timeframe serves as a critical boundary for the validity of the contract (sahih) versus its nullification (batil), reflecting the principle of clarity in commercial exchanges to avoid *gharar* (uncertainty).
